Messages.Body:
Charles Richard Robb (cr...@Ra.MsState.Edu) wrote:
: I don;t see the big fuss about the new backs..

Let me explain...

: Tom' press release said that the cards will be allowed in combination for

: tournaments and that the change shoudl not affect the compatability.

WotC has changed their minds ( or lied? ) about the card back issues before,
so the fact that they _said_ that the cards would be usable in tournaments
does not mean they _will_ be usable in tournaments. Think about it this way:
There are people who will take advantage of the ability to mark their cards,
because there are people who suck. People who run tournaments will be far too
busy to check every crypt and library for certain patterns of cards that might
be contrued as cheating. Therefore, if cards are allowed to be mixed in
tournaments, the cheaters will an advantage.

: For

: everyday playing, who cares if the cards are mixed?

How about this: We are both playing Tremere, you have Bob, a Dark Soveriegns
Tremere in play, as well as Sarah Cobbler. I play Betrayer. All my crypt
cards are Jyhad cards. Guess you know who the traitor is. In general you
will always know which cards are _not_ expansion set cards, even in friendly
games. It's even worse for people like me, who have enough Jyhad cards, and
was only planning on bying the expansions. With me you'll know it's an
expansion card, just from the card backs ( he can't be holding any wakes,
those are all V:TES cards. ).

: And with tournaments,

: it is said that judges will be looking for people who mark cards by using
: the backs to their advantage. If you have hundreds of dollars or other
: currency
: imnvested in the game, you still can play with what you have so get over it.

If you have hundreds of dollars invested in alpha cards, you still don't have a
mana drain, which is a very useful tournament card. The same will be true for
V:TES.

: If they wanted you to have to buy more cards then WotC would have made them

: incompatible qith the new cards.

They already did that. None of my Jyhad cards are compatible with my Magic:
the Gathering cards. The problem is not them releasing a new game ( V:TES ),
the problem is, they will no longer be supporting an old game ( Jyhad ). I
can still buy Magic expansion sets now that Jyhad has come out. If I was able
to buy Dark Soveriegns with the Jyhad back, I would care less is they replaced
all the Jyhad vampires with movie shots from Interview with the Vampire when
they relaesd V:TES.

: And if you're so anal retentive that all of
: your backs must match....tough!

This many people don't post about a subject if their only desire is to be
neat. Mabybe you don't expect respect from WotC, because you have no respect
for other people.

Larrx...

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Larry Harriman <la...@bu.edu> wrote:
>WotC has changed their minds ( or lied? ) about the card back issues before,

Yes, we changed our minds before setting the final policy on the card
backs. The only firm policy released on the card backs was the one
recently announced, saying that the card backs will change.

>so the fact that they _said_ that the cards would be usable in tournaments

>does not mean they _will_ be usable in tournaments...

I have seen the Convocation rules for Jyhad/V:TES, and they explicitly
allow mixing the card backs. I see no reason for this to change before
those rules are released.

>...People who run tournaments will be far too

>busy to check every crypt and library for certain patterns of cards that might

>be contrued as cheating...

We never expect the judges to policy each and every deck for cheating.
We don't expect them to check each and every deck to make sure it meets
the deck construction rules, for example. It is left up to the player to
spot potential cheating, and to bring it to the attention of a
referee or judge.

>How about this: We are both playing Tremere, you have Bob, a Dark Soveriegns
>Tremere in play, as well as Sarah Cobbler. I play Betrayer. All my crypt

>cards are Jyhad cards. Guess you know who the traitor is...

OK, so you find out in one turn instead of two. What's the big deal?

>It's even worse for people like me, who have enough Jyhad cards, and
>was only planning on bying the expansions. With me you'll know it's an
>expansion card, just from the card backs ( he can't be holding any wakes,
>those are all V:TES cards. ).

Well, is there anything that says you have to show them the backs of
the cards in your hand? It's not clear what the answer to this would be
in official tournament play, so it strikes me as perfectly reasonable
to disallow that sort of examination, especially in non-tournament play.

>The problem is not them releasing a new game ( V:TES ),

>the problem is, they will no longer be supporting an old game ( Jyhad )...

V:TES is Jyhad, just repackaged. By supporting V:TES we are supporting Jyhad.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

Messages.Author: Aaron Mandelbaum
Messages.Body:
cr...@Ra.MsState.Edu (Charles Richard Robb) writes:

>Respect?
>Where's repsect when it comes to selling more of your product for capital
>gain? This is capitalism. That's the way things work.

Or 'don't work,' as the case may be. 'Respect' from a capitalistic viewpoint
is an intangible quality which may have a dollar value placed on it or not,
at your discretion. If customers demand 'respect', then it's profitable to
offer it. If they'll buy from you no matter what, screw 'em.

>If you don't like changes to a

>product, don;t buy it. I might buy the expansions just to make straight
>expansion decks and not mix them with other 'alpha' cards.

Then you're a fool, since it's highly unlikely that 'all expansion' decks
will work. So you'll be left with marked expansion cards which you can't
really play with.

It's people like you who turn capitalism into a self-serving dickensian hell.

>Many who want alpha
>cards will trade beta cards to get alpha with those who need betas so that
>their decks will be indistinguishable from the rest of the cards.

*Why* would anyone in their right mind trade betas for alphas? Players, I'm
talking about here, since collectors can hardly support everyone's need for
a good mix of betas. If you offer a player with all betas an alpha sengir
dagger for a pair of beta wolf-claws, he'd be a fool to accept since he
couldn't use it. Or, assuming that the people he knows aren't fools, trade
it for anything beta which he could use.

You'll either be buying your betas or doing without, or finding some idiot
to be dragged down into marked-back hell with you to get halfway out.

Good luck.

--
Aaron Mandelbaum

bit and see what a problem this would cause, maybe not in this situation,
but in similar ones?

Fine. Let's say that you have TEN vampires out, not three. So you find
out in one turn instead of nine. Is that a big enough deal?

It's not just one card, like Betrayer, not just one example that you can

lack of respect for your existing customer base.

address them, try using this phrase next time:

"So what?"

It means the same thing as "what's the big deal", but it's a bit more honest.

Bye now.

>but in similar ones?

>out in one turn instead of nine. Is that a big enough deal?

I considered situations where more than two vampires in play, but how many
more vampires is the person really likely to have? How often do you see
people with ten vampires in play? Three to five is probably the average
range, once the game gets going.

>It's not just one card, like Betrayer, not just one example that you can
>find a way to discredit. It's a whole range of unbalancing situations.

By and large, these unbalancing situations only seem that way if you don't
consider how the knowledge can be used against you. In another post, someone
suggested having your untap cards marked. Great, so you know when your
untap cards are going to come up. This can easily lead to taking actions
prematurely just so you can get to your untap cards, taking bleed actions
that just get bounced and allow your prey to whack your grandprey that
much sooner, falling into a combat deck waiting to cycle its hand, etc.

>Since it's clear that you'd rather dismiss our concerns rather than

>address them...

The fact that we are changing the card backs does not mean that we ignored
the feedback from the customers. We considered the feedback carefully,
along with our own thoughts, and decided to change the card backs anyway.
This is hardly what I'd call "dismissing" the concerns, but maybe I just
have a skewed defintion of "dismiss".

>It means the same thing as "what's the big deal"...

"What's the big deal" (while not a great thing to post) was specifically
referring to the Betrayer example, not to the issue in general.

Usually nobody means the Convocation rules when they make a statement
like this. The rules say its okay, but the expected reaction is that the
mixed decks will be outlawed "...to make my life easier as a tournament
sponsor..."

> >...People who run tournaments will be far too busy to check every
> >crypt and library for certain patterns of cards that might

> >be construed as cheating...

And so they will do away with the "problem" that they see, which is
mixed decks.

> >How about this: We are both playing Tremere, you have Bob, a Dark Soveriegns
> >Tremere in play, as well as Sarah Cobbler. I play Betrayer. All my crypt
> >cards are Jyhad cards. Guess you know who the traitor is...
>
> OK, so you find out in one turn instead of two. What's the big deal?

Well in just about any game, if you lose an amount of blood that is half
as much as I intended, you are much better off. I have lost an advantage
that I hoped to gain by playing the card in the first place. (If you did
not know which was Betrayed, you would have to guess the second time as
well as the first, in order to remove the Betrayer. With a difference in
backs, that cannot happen.)

> >It's even worse for people like me, who have enough Jyhad cards, and
> >was only planning on bying the expansions. With me you'll know it's an
> >expansion card, just from the card backs ( he can't be holding any wakes,
> >those are all V:TES cards. ).
>
> Well, is there anything that says you have to show them the backs of
> the cards in your hand? It's not clear what the answer to this would be
> in official tournament play, so it strikes me as perfectly reasonable
> to disallow that sort of examination, especially in non-tournament play.

In all the rules I have seen the Convocation come up with, (as well as
other non-santioned tourneys) you are required to keep your cards (and
your hands) above the level of the table, or risk disqualification. Thus
your cards are visible. And if you want to look at them yourself, your
opponant will see the backs. (Unless you want to look silly trying to
hide the front AND the back of each card while you look at them.)

> >The problem is not them releasing a new game ( V:TES ),
> >the problem is, they will no longer be supporting an old game ( Jyhad )...
>

> V:TES is Jyhad, just repackaged. By supporting V:TES we are supporting Jyhad.

>
>
> Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
> aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.
>
>

As often as you try to sell us the "same game" story, you will be
contradicting yourself. They have the same rules (if the new players use
all the rules, not just the Magic:tG rules), but they are distinct in
their presentation. This unfortunately makes them different enough to
make mixing them problematic at best.
